## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Indiana NWEA MAP Assessment Administration
• NWEA provided Indiana DOE with NWEA MAP assessment data
 from their Fall 2020-2021 and Winter 2020-2021 administration
 windows. (??? Dates for the administration windows, who tested
 remotely versus in-person)
• NWEA MAP assessment data consisted primarily of Language
 Arts and Mathematics data. There were minor case counts in
 Science.
• NWEA MAP data existed for Grades K to 10
• Statewide participation in NWEA MAP assessments approached
 and, in most cases, exceeded 40% in all grades except 9 and 10
 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Pandemic related academic impact
• Due to school disruption, it is commonly believed that students have been negatively
 impacted academically.
• If we think of a student progressing forward academically, the pandemic has, by and
 large, acted like a headwind, slowing the academic progress of students.
• Academic impact (sometimes referred to learning loss or unfinished learning) is the
 difference between where the student’s academic attainment would have been had the
 pandemic not happened and where the student’s academic attainment actually was.
• Two ways of examining academic impact:
 • Status comparisons (how does current status for a group (e.g., 4th graders) compare to that group (4th
 graders) in the past. Assumes comparable groups.
 • Growth comparisons (how does current growth for a group (e.g., 4th graders) compare to that group
 (4th graders) in the past. Assumes comparable groups.

 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 4</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Pandemic related academic impact
• Because we only have Fall 2020-2021 and Winter 2020-2021 data we cannot
 perform status comparisons with historical data.
• We are similarly impeded with growth data but because growth percentiles
 (nationally) have a mean/median of 50, we can look at deviations from 50 as a
 rough estimate of the academic impact.
• Ideally, instead of 50 we would use historical growth mean/median growth
 percentiles for Indiana to determine how current growth deviates from historical
 growth.
• We will proceed with this line of analysis/reasoning with the hope of tightening
 the analyses going forward with additional historical data.

 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 5</div>
```

```{=html}
• NWEA MAP assessment data provides several student growth

• NWEA MAP assessments are given 3 times a year leading to
 several growth scenarios:
 • Fall to Fall
 • Fall to Winter
 • Fall to Spring
 • Winter to Winter
 • Winter to Fall (not calculated)
 • …
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/16.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Interpretation of growth results
• NOTE: We assume normal growth in Indian pre-COVID was
 approximately 50.
• Deviation from 50 is indicative of academic impact/learning loss.
• A change in mean SGP of 5 corresponds to an effect size of 0.18
• Roughly (trying to translate into time):
 • Effect size &gt;= 0.6 (mean SGP &lt; 35): 12+ weeks behind
 • 0.45 &lt; Effect size &lt; 0.6 (35 &lt; mean SGP &lt; 40): 8-11 weeks behind
 • 0.2 &lt; Effect size &lt; 0.45 (40 &lt; mean SGP &lt; 45): 3 to 8 weeks behind
 • Effect size &lt; 0.2 (mean SGP &gt;=45): Less than 3 weeks behind
 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 16</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/17.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Summary of growth results
• Academic impact was more substantial in mathematics than in
 language arts.
 • One hypothesis for the lesser impact in language arts than in
 mathematics is that language arts is more easily “taught” at home.
 • Another hypothesis for the lesser impact in language arts is that the
 NWEA MAP assessment don’t address the content standards to the
 same depth as would a state summative assessment.
• Academic impact was slightly larger in lower grades than in upper
 grades.
• Results are consistent with what has been observed in other
 states.
 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 17</div>
```
